etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French mutuel, from Latin mūtuus.

definitions.definition: Having the same relationship, each to each other.
Collective, done or held in common.

quote.citation: 1809, Faculty of Advocates (Scotland), Decisions of the Court of Sessions, from 1752 to 1808, page 216:
quote.text: On his area the pursuer built a dwelling-house, of which the gable and garden-wall were mutual with his neighbour Smith  […]

definitions.definition: (Relating to a company, insurance or financial institution) Owned by the members.
(Internet) Either of a pair of people who follow each other's social media accounts.
